Search and rescue teams are still searching for the pilot and a passenger on board the Cessna aircraft that reportedly crashed on Wednesday, the Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines (CAAP) said.

CAAP spokesman Eric Apolonio said they are waiting for the official reports from the CAAP's  Aircraft Accident Investigation and Inquiry Board (AAIIB), who are on the ground searching for the two persons on board the Cessna plane with registry number RP-C2444.

"May nakitang wreckage ang mga residents malapit sa area pero hindi masabi kung [iyon] nga 'yung wreckage ng Cessna kaya andun ['yung] AAIIB personnel," Apolonio said.

CAAP Surigao del Norte officials said that local officials are still conducting search operations for the two persons on board the ill-fated Cessna aircraft RP-C2444 that was reported missing.

Unofficial report that the wreckage of the Cessna plane RPC2444  was found by the retrieval team of the Dinagat rescue team, but the pilot and the passenger have not yet been found. This is being verified by AAIIB.

As of 5:00 PM Thursday, no official reports about the wreckage have been released, and the pilot and lone passenger remain missing, Apolonio added. | via Rodolfo Santos

• Brown Street and South Street
• Brown Street and Nichols Street

There are no reported injuries at this time. Please avoid the area and seek alternate routes. Updates will be provided when the roadway reopens.
